subject: Next steps: DPA clarifications & evidence for Medix Health pilot
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Somas <jane.somas@medixhealth.com>, Medix Health Security Team <secops@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — DPA roles, residency & logging

Hi Jane / SecOps team,

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciate the clear framing of your pilot objectives and your privacy constraints. Quick recap + asks so we stay aligned: 

- Scope: real‑time inference for anonymized patient summaries (PII minimization required).
- Data residency: production inference must run in us‑east-1; logs may be replicated for monitoring but must not contain raw PHI.
- Retention: Medix would like a 30‑day rolling token-level log retention and the ability to request shorter retention for specific datasets.
- Notifications: ask for 48‑hour notify window for subprocessor breaches (minimum), and immediate escalation to your security contact on suspected PHI exposure.

Immediate asks from our side: could you confirm whether Medix needs Redwood to be listed as a "processor" or as a co-controller for this pilot? That will guide the DPA redline. Also: please confirm whether the 30‑day retention requirement is flexible for logs that are purely operational (metrics only).

Attaching a marked‑up DPA draft that highlights the controller/processor language and proposed notify timeline. I also attached our latest SOC 2 report for your security review.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_markup_v1.pdf (DPA with comments), SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-Report-2026.pdf (redacted sections allowed for review)

Next steps I propose: 
- SecOps to confirm controller vs. processor stance and residency requirement (by EOD Tuesday).
- If you need a legal redline, we can schedule a short sync with our legal ops (30 min).
- Connor to follow up with technical evidence for log redaction & KV cache controls.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Jane Somas <jane.somas@medixhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — DPA roles, residency & logging

Connor — thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick answers from SecOps perspective: 

- Controller vs processor: For the pilot, Medix will treat Redwood as a processor. We will escalate if scope changes.
- Residency: us‑east-1 is required for production inference. Acceptable.
- Retention: 30 days is our preference but we need the ability for ad‑hoc shorter retention windows per dataset.
- Notifications: 48 hours for subprocessor events is our baseline; immediate phone escalation for suspected PHI exfiltration.

Couple of asks before we move to legal redline: 
1) Can you confirm whether operational logs (latency, errors) ever contain de‑identified tokens or only numeric/aggregated metrics?
2) Do you provide an auditable log of subprocessor list and change history? We need to map that to our vendor register.

If you can confirm the two items and share the SOC2, we can loop in procurement/legal for a redline next week.

Thanks,
Jane Somas
Director, Security Governance
Medix Health
secops@medixhealth.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up from today's discovery — DPA roles, residency & logging

Marissa / Rachel — forwarding Medix's replies (below). Two quick asks so we can respond cleanly: 

1) Rachel — can you confirm the canonical answer on whether our operational logs ever contain token texts? My understanding: latency/error traces never include token content; exceptions during model decode may capture short snippets unless prefix suppression is enabled. We should provide a short paragraph describing KV cache redaction + prefix stripping and whether we can configure zero‑token logging for this customer.

2) Marissa — procurement/legal will likely ask for a full subprocessor list and change notification cadence. Do we have a published subprocessor register we can share and an internal SLA for notification of additions/removals? If so, please point to the doc or attach.

Attachments included for Medix: redwood_dpa_markup_v1.pdf, SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-Report-2026.pdf

Below is the thread to include in the reply to Medix. I can send to them once I have the two bullets answered. 

Thanks — planning to propose a 30‑minute redline call on Monday (12:00 PT) if that works.

—Connor

Jane — quick update and answers to your two questions after checking with the team: 

1) Operational logs: by default our production telemetry (latency, error codes, host metrics) does not include token strings. Token text may appear only in exception traces when model decode fails; for the pilot we can enable a zero‑token logging policy that suppresses token content in all traces. We'll document the configuration and provide a short checklist for your engineers.

2) Subprocessor register: we maintain a living register and publish change history. Link below points to the current list; we'll also add a weekly change digest for procurement if that helps.

Links / attachments: 
- SOC 2 report (attached)

- I will schedule a 30‑minute redline call for Monday 12:00 PT (tentative) — please ping if a different time works.
- Marissa will share subprocessor register and notification cadence.
- Rachel will prepare a 1‑page technical note on KV cache redaction and zero‑token logging config.

If that all looks good I'll send the calendar invite and a single PDF that bundles the DPA mark‑up + SOC2 for your legal team.

Best,
